# Task Board
A simple kanban task app with To Do, In Progress, and Done columns. Create tasks with a priority and optional due date, move them across the board, and see counts plus an overdue badge at a glance. No external APIs.
## Data Model
![ER Diagram](docs/notes/er_diagram.png)
The data model consists of two main entities: `Project` and `Task`.
- **Project**: Represents a container for tasks. Each project has a name, an owner (a `User`), and a description. - **Task**: Represents a single task within a project. Each task has a title, description, priority, status, and an optional due date.
This model allows for organizing tasks into different projects, with a clear ownership structure.

# Ideas & Selection Rationale - Assignment ideas: Task Board - Simple kanban workflow, clear task management, minimal dependencies
# Wireframe Notes - Goal of v1 wireframes: Keep it tiny and shippable. Prioritize task board with three columns (To Do, In Progress, Done) + simple task creation. - Screens included: - Board view: three-column kanban layout with task cards showing title, priority, due date - Create/Edit task: form with title, description, priority dropdown, optional due date - Empty/Error: first-run blank state, basic validation errors
# Branching Strategy - Strategy chosen: Simple Gitflow - main (protected, demo-ready) - develop (integration) - feature/ per weekly topic -> merge back to develop - release/ before demos -> merge to main - hotfix/ from main for urgent fixes -> merge back to develop
- Planned feature branches (Task Board): - feature/models -> feature/crud -> feature/ui -> feature/board -> feature/admin
# Django Setup (Task Board) - startproject folder name chosen: appserver; app name: tasks — simple and clear for task management.
# Data Model Design - **Models Created**: `Project` and `Task`. - **Fields**: - `Project`: `name`, `description`, `owner`, `created_at`. - `Task`: `title`, `description`, `project`, `priority`, `status`, `due_date`, `created_at`, `updated_at`. - **Relationships**: - `Task.project`: A `ForeignKey` to `Project`. This creates a one-to-many relationship where a project can have multiple tasks. `on_delete=models.CASCADE` was chosen so that if a project is deleted, all its associated tasks are also deleted. This keeps the database clean and avoids orphaned tasks. - `Project.owner`: A `ForeignKey` to the `User` model. This assigns ownership of a project to a user. `on_delete=models.CASCADE` means if a user is deleted, their projects (and by extension, their tasks) are also deleted. - **Constraints**: - `UniqueConstraint(fields=['project', 'title'], name='unique_task_title_in_project')` in the `Task` model ensures that no two tasks within the same project can have the same title. This prevents duplicate tasks. - `ordering = ["name"]` in `Project` and `ordering = ["status", "-priority", "due_date", "-created_at"]` in `Task` provide default sorting for querysets, which is useful for consistent presentation. - **Seeding Data**: - A superuser was created to own the projects. - Two projects were created: "Website Redesign" and "Mobile App Development". - Several tasks were created for each project with different priorities, statuses, and due dates to simulate a real-world scenario. - A duplicate task was attempted to be created to test the `UniqueConstraint`.
# Virtual Environment Choice - Using Python venv because it's simple and works with PyCharm auto-detect.

# Assignment 4 - Django Views Implementation
## Why I Wrote Two Views - **HttpResponse View (task_stats)**: Demonstrates manual HTML construction without Django's template system. This shows the low-level approach where you have complete control over the HTML output but must handle everything manually. - **render() View (task_board)**: Uses Django's template system with context passing. This is the preferred Django approach as it separates logic from presentation and enables template inheritance.
## Differences Between HttpResponse and render() - **HttpResponse**: Returns raw HTML strings constructed in Python. Requires manual HTML escaping and styling. Good for simple responses or API endpoints. Less maintainable for complex pages. - **render()**: Uses Django templates with context dictionaries. Supports template inheritance, filters, tags, and automatic HTML escaping. More maintainable and follows Django best practices.
## URL and Template Decisions - **Separate URLs**: Created distinct URLs (/tasks/stats/ and /tasks/) to clearly demonstrate both approaches working independently. - **Template Inheritance**: Used base.html with {% block %} structure to maintain consistent navigation and styling across all pages. - **{% for %} with {% empty %}**: Implemented in all list templates to gracefully handle empty querysets with user-friendly messages. - **Context Strategy**: Passed multiple querysets in render() view to organize tasks by status, enabling the kanban board layout.
## Key Learning Points - HttpResponse requires manual work but gives complete control - render() leverages Django's powerful template system for cleaner, more maintainable code - Both approaches can use the same underlying data and business logic - Template inheritance eliminates code duplication across pages
